$comment: DELIBERATELY DORMANT DEPLOY PATHS — consumed by scripts/ci/_deploy-path-disposition.mjs
and reported by scripts/ci/check-deploy-staleness.mjs.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS (#4144). deploy-staleness reported six untracked stale or
never-run deploy paths on every run and nothing in the repo recorded a decision about
any of them, so it reported them daily into a void. deploy-integrity.md R1 and R3 both
say that is not an acceptable steady state — but the fix is not 'make it green'. A
report that is permanently red for reasons nobody has decided about is a report nobody
reads, which is exactly how the 2026-08-05 two-week deploy blackout stayed invisible.
So the missing fact is INTENT. 'Stale because nobody looked' and 'stale because we
decided to hold it, for this measured reason, until this date' are different facts with
different fixes, and until this register they rendered identically.
AN ENTRY DOES NOT MAKE A ROW GREEN. An acknowledged path is PRINTED on every run with
its owner, reason, acknowledged condition and expiry — reported as ACK, never omitted,
never counted as ok. The only thing it changes is the exit code for that one row.
RULES (enforced by _deploy-path-disposition.mjs, not by convention). Every one resolves
to NOT-ACKNOWLEDGING on failure, so a malformed entry can never silence a lane by
accident — it just stops suppressing, and the check prints which rule it failed:
1. `workflow` must match a WATCHED entry in check-deploy-staleness.mjs exactly. An
entry for an unwatched lane is a FINDING (it acknowledges nothing while reading as
a decision), not a silent no-op.
2. `disposition` must be `dispatch-only` or `retirement-proposed`. There is
deliberately NO value meaning 'this runs automatically': a lane with a working
trigger needs no entry here, and inventing one would let a broken trigger hide
behind a word.
3. `owner` is required. A dormant deploy path has an owner, not just a note.
4. `reason` must be at least 60 characters and free of TODO/TBD/WIP placeholders.
State what was MEASURED and what must be true to change the disposition. Do not
state a cause you did not establish (.claude/rules/deploy-integrity.md R7).
5. `declaredOn` (YYYY-MM-DD) is required and must not be in the future.
6. `reviewBy` (YYYY-MM-DD) is required, must be after `declaredOn`, and EXPIRES. Past
its date the lane reads as undeclared and the row goes red again. Without an expiry
a dormant path becomes a permanent one with nobody deciding to make it so.
7. `acknowledges` must be a non-empty subset of [never-run, drift]. `failing`,
`disabled`, `state-unknown` and `query-failed` can NEVER be signed off here: a
failing lane is deploy-integrity R1, a switched-off lane has its own register
(workflow-lane-states-allowlist.json), and the other two are unmeasured rather than
decided. Naming one refuses the WHOLE entry, so a forbidden condition cannot ride
along beside a legal one.
DRAINING HAS TEETH. An entry for a lane that is not watched, a duplicate, or a
`never-run` acknowledgment on a lane that has since run, is a FINDING that fails the
check. A register nobody drains stops describing reality. A `drift` acknowledgment is
deliberately not audited that way — drift oscillates — it expires on `reviewBy` instead.

dispositions.reason: IL5 IS DECLARED UNVERIFIED, NOT IMPLIED WORKING (cloud-parity.md: an untested boundary is named as untested). This lane has never executed, so nothing about the DoD IL5 estate has ever been measured in either direction. It stays dispatch-only, and a schedule would be actively harmful: MEASURED 2026-09-01, `gh api repos/fgarofalo56/csa-inabox/environments` reports the `il5-deploy` environment carrying a required_reviewers protection rule, and this workflow's `deploy-validate` job runs in it. A cron on a reviewer-gated environment produces runs that park at `waiting` and execute nothing, stacking one per day — that is happening to deploy-fiab-gcch right now (#4233), so adding one here would convert an honest never-run row into a queue of runs that also deploy nothing. The first IL5 run is an operator dispatch into a sovereign subscription with a human approval, per the same reasoning #4144 gives for not dispatching during triage. TO CHANGE THIS: dispatch the lane (run_mode=whatif-only first — its default already applies nothing and carries the DRY RUN marker, so it cannot clear this row falsely), then drain this entry once a real apply has run.

This lane builds the loom-unity image on the Gov ACR and deploys it plus the Purview wiring into the GCC-High estate, and that estate is DELIBERATELY STOPPED. MEASURED: scripts/ci/estate-pause-declaration.json declares boundary GCC-High paused by fgarofalo56, declaredOn 2026-08-26, reviewBy 2026-11-24, on the strength of deploy-fiab-gcch failing 17 consecutive runs at the ADX preflight with byte-identical output. An automatic trigger here would build and deploy into that stopped estate from an unattended run, which is the exact outcome reconcileWithDeclaredPause refuses for the ADX cluster ('a start would defeat the pause mandate and bill the operator from an unattended cron'). Dispatch stays the only trigger while the pause stands. This `reviewBy` is deliberately the pause declaration's own date so the two cannot drift apart: when the pause is lifted or renewed, this decision is re-made with it. TO CHANGE THIS: resume the Gov estate, dispatch this lane once to land the accumulated wiring, then re-decide whether it earns an automatic trigger.

Shipping this image requires a per-run human security acceptance that no trigger can supply, so an automatic trigger would produce a lane that is red by construction rather than a lane that deploys. MEASURED (recorded in the workflow's own header, scanned 2026-08-02 with --ignore-unfixed --severity CRITICAL): the upstream delta-sharing payload's jars carry 38 CRITICAL findings that no packaging change clears, upstream has published no image since April 2024, and .trivyignore is deliberately empty. The lane therefore REPORTS and REFUSES unless the dispatcher sets `accept_upstream_cves`, which defaults false and is recorded in the run title. On a push or schedule event that input is empty, so every automatic run would fail the Trivy gate after having already pushed the image — a permanently red lane whose redness says nothing about drift. Accepting 38 unfixable upstream CRITICALs is a reviewed operator decision, not a workflow default. TO CHANGE THIS: an upstream rebuild that clears the findings, or a Loom-built server image, removes the acceptance and with it this disposition.
